A_target.statement:
Let $T$ be a [[Definition:Hyperbolic Triangle|triangle]] in the [[Definition:Hyperbolic Plane|hyperbolic plane]] of curvature $-1$ with angles $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$.
Then:
:$\map {\operatorname {Area} } T = \pi - \paren {\alpha + \beta + \gamma}$
so the angle sum is less than $\pi$ and every triangle has area less than $\pi$.

B_source.statement:
Let $T$ be a [[Definition:Geodesic Triangle|geodesic triangle]] with angles $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ on a surface with [[Definition:Gaussian Curvature|Gaussian curvature]] $K$.
Then:
:$\displaystyle \alpha + \beta + \gamma - \pi = \int_T K \rd A$

object_map.reformulation: Specialize the local Gauss-Bonnet formula to constant negative curvature.

validity_conditions: Hyperbolic lines are geodesics, so hyperbolic triangles are geodesic triangles.
With constant curvature +1 the same specialization gives Girard's spherical excess formula.
proof_plan:
By the [[Gauss-Bonnet Theorem|local Gauss-Bonnet formula]]:
:$\alpha + \beta + \gamma - \pi = -\map {\operatorname {Area} } T$
